Simulation on AUD-USD:

I used a free version of simulation software from FXCM, and it is useful but has a lot of bugs. One of the bugs happens when my entry order doesn't get triggered despite getting reached. That happened in this scenario, but I wanted to show the top down analysis of the trade anyway..it is a great example.

Like my oil trade above, I began by finding a HTF IQM.

Next, drop down to LTF and look for another IQM or other important PA that supports a possible long trade.

My main focus at this point is setting up the best trade with the lowest risk and highest return. I look at the last candle to cross the HTF IQM and I draw the range of that candle. As you can see from the chart below, the candle has a large range (44 pips). I look at every scale from 1-min to 30-min to draw a conservative candle...I place my stop loss just below the low of the candle on the 30 min scale... (In this example, the 30-min candle's low and the 1-min candle's low is the same)

The ideal place to go long is at the yellow shaded area where the black and red horizontal lines exist. But here is where MM and trade psychology comes in: I have to be aware of the necessary location of my stop loss. This stop loss has to be located below the low of the black box - and if I set an entry order to buy at the yellow shaded region, my SL is approximately 20 pips. This is too wide of a stop loss for my trading strategy. I am looking for a minimum 1:3 RR - but would rather see closer to 1:4 RR. In keeping consistent with my MM goal, an entry at the yellow zone requires a target to be located 60-80 pips from my entry - too ambitious. I want low risk high return trades. The only way to manage this trade properly (under my MM requirements) is to set my entry order no more than 11 pips from the SL. I do this specifically because my target for this trade is approx 35 pips away from the proposed entry. I accept the possibility that price will bounce at the yellow zone and leave me in the dust. I am OK with missing out on trades.

An important point regarding the target: I don't know my target until price unfolds and comes very close to my entry point. This can be complicated, since the entry is dependent on the SL but the SL is somewhat dependent on my proposed target. This is why it is important to watch trades as they unfold as opposed to setting a limit order and walking away. As price unfolds, I see a nice supply zone forming just before price takes a dive to my entry.

The chart below shows where my entry, SL, and target is located. As you can see, my simulation software didn't trigger like it should have..that said, it is easy to see how the trade would have turned out.

I know the entry above looks too good to be true...It is my humble opinion that predicting exact areas where price will turn is not always possible. I simply got lucky on this entry...price could have easily missed my entry by a couple of pips and there are times when this happens. In my opinion, this is why trading psychology is so important: the fear of missing out on a trade shouldn't cause a trader to execute a trade that is beyond the scope of their MM requirements. It takes practice but over time a trader can train themselves to shut off their emotions. I still struggle with this, but I am getting a lot better at it.

شبیه‌سازی روی AUD-USD:

نسخهٔ رایگان نرم‌افزار شبیه‌سازی FXCM را استفاده کردم که مفید است اما باگ‌های زیادی دارد. یکی از باگ‌ها وقتی رخ می‌دهد که سفارش ورودم با وجود رسیدن فعال نمی‌شود. در این سناریو همین اتفاق افتاد، اما می‌خواستم تحلیل top-down معامله را به هر حال نشان دهم… مثال عالی است.

مثل معاملهٔ نفتی‌ام بالا، با یافتن یک IQM تایم‌فریم بالاتر شروع کردم.

بعد، به LTF می‌روم و دنبال IQM دیگری یا PA مهم دیگری می‌گردم که از خرید احتمالی حمایت کند.

تمرکز اصلی‌ام در این نقطه ستاپ بهترین معامله با کمترین ریسک و بالاترین بازده است. به آخرین کندلِ عبورکننده از IQM تایم‌فریم بالاتر نگاه می‌کنم و بازهٔ آن کندل را می‌کشم. همان‌طور که از نمودار پایین می‌بینید، کندل بازهٔ بزرگی دارد (44 پیپ). همهٔ مقیاس‌ها را از 1 دقیقه تا 30 دقیقه نگاه می‌کنم تا کندل محافظه‌کارانه‌ای بکشم… حد ضرر‌ام را درست زیر کف کندل روی مقیاس 30 دقیقه‌ای می‌گذارم… (در این مثال، کف کندل 30 دقیقه‌ای و کف کندل 1 دقیقه‌ای یکی است)

بهترین جای خرید در ناحیهٔ سایه‌زنی زرد است که خطوط افقی سیاه و قرمز در آن واقع شده‌اند. اما این‌جاست که MM و روان‌شناسی معامله وارد می‌شود: باید از محل لازم برای حد ضرر‌ام آگاه باشم. این حد ضرر باید زیر کف جعبهٔ سیاه باشد - و اگر سفارش ورودی برای خرید در ناحیهٔ سایه‌زنی زرد بگذارم، SL من تقریباً 20 پیپ است. این برای استراتژی معاملاتی‌ام حد ضرر خیلی پهنی است. به دنبال حداقل 1:3 R:R هستم - اما ترجیح می‌دهم نزدیک 1:4 R:R ببینم. در راستای هدف MM‌م، ورود در ناحیهٔ زرد تارگتی می‌خواهد که 60-80 پیپ از ورودم دور باشد - خیلی جاه‌طلبانه. معاملات کم‌ریسک با بازده بالا می‌خواهم. تنها راه برای مدیریت درست این معامله (طبق الزامات MM‌م) گذاشتن سفارش ورود حداکثر 11 پیپ از SL است. این را مخصوصاً انجام می‌دهم چون تارگتم برای این معامله تقریباً 35 پیپ از ورود پیشنهادی دور است. احتمال اینکه قیمت در ناحیهٔ زرد برگردد و دستم را به هوا بدهد می‌پذیرم. از دست دادن معاملات برام مشکلی نیست.

نکتهٔ مهم دربارهٔ تارگت: تارگتم را نمی‌دانم تا وقتی قیمت پیش می‌رود و خیلی به نقطهٔ ورودم نزدیک می‌شود. این می‌تواند پیچیده باشد، چون ورود به SL بستگی دارد اما SL تا حدی به تارگت پیشنهادی‌ام بستگی دارد. به همین دلیل مهم است که معاملات را در حین پیش رفتن تماشا کنیم به‌جای گذاشتن سفارش لیمیت و رفتن. وقتی قیمت پیش می‌رود، ناحیهٔ عرضهٔ خوبی را درست قبل از اینکه قیمت به ورودم فرو برود می‌بینم.

نمودار پایین نشان می‌دهد ورود، SL و تارگتم کجا قرار دارند. همان‌طور که می‌بینید، نرم‌افزار شبیه‌سازی‌ام مثل باید فعال نشد… با این حال، آسان است ببینیم معامله چطور تمام می‌شد.

می‌دانم این ورود برای باور کردن زیادی خوب است… نظر فروتنانهٔ من این است که پیش‌بینی نواحی دقیقِ برگشت قیمت همیشه ممکن نیست. فقط در این ورود شانس آوردم… قیمت به‌راحتی می‌توانست چند پیپ از ورودم رد شود و گاهی همین اتفاق می‌افتد. به نظر من، به همین دلیل روان‌شناسی معامله مهم است: ترس از جا ماندن نباید معامله‌گر را وادارد معامله‌ای فراتر از محدودهٔ الزامات MM‌ش اجرا کند. تمرین می‌خواهد اما با زمان معامله‌گر می‌تواند خودش را طوری تربیت کند که احساساتش را خاموش کند. هنوز با این مشکل دارم، اما خیلی بهتر شده‌ام.

I currently have a buy order set for GBP-USD. Here is a top down analysis of the current setup.

HTF:

LTF confirmation of IQM. There are two areas of interest shown by yellow circles.

The range of the blue rectangle is too large...at approximately (21 pips). I need to reduce the risk, especially depending on where I expect the target to be located

My stop loss is shown on the chart below - the stop loss is located just beneath the low of the last 30 min candle to cross the HTF IQM line (black horizontal) and the LTF IQM (solid red line). Notes on the chart reiterate the issue with setting my entry order at the top of the yellow shaded rectangle.

The target (and the entry) is not set in stone at this point - the reason for this is I cannot set my entry unless I feel confident where my target is located, and I can't feel comfortable about the location of my target until I see more PA unfold. Specifically, I want to see PA as it approaches my entry. At this stage, I see the future downside break of the "FL" labeled on the chart below as the most likely area where my long position will encounter a substantial set of sell orders that could bounce price lower. Depending on how the PA develops as price approached my entry, the target may shorten. If so, my entry will likely be adjusted lower as well - to decrease the risk between my entry and the stop loss. My current entry order is set in an area that requires a 14-pip stop loss. This is a high stop loss for me - usually I like my stop loss to be at or under 10 pips. My requirement for a target is minimum 3X risk. In this case, the target is located approximately 64 pips from the entry (roughly 4.5 R). If my target drops, my entry will drop accordingly. My stop loss will not change.

A quick note regarding my methodology for entry (I am still in the process of refining my standard approach to setting an entry order): I understand price may bounce prior to price reaching my entry - in fact, this happens on a regular basis. I have decided to sacrifice good trading opportunities for a strict risk management plan. I am OK with missing out on trades but I am not OK with taking on too much risk Years ago I lost a very large live account over the course of a few short months. That is NEVER happening again. The main reason I don't adjust my positioning size instead (as opposed to adjusting my entry to control risk) is the issue of my target - wide stop losses require an equally wide target in order to meet my 3X risk/return requirement. My core specialty will be executing low risk short-term 'opportunity' trades. Once the SL exceeds 10 pips, my target requirement exceeds 30-40 pips, and it takes longer for the trade to complete, which exposes my trade to increased external risk.

حد ضرر‌ام روی نمودار پایین نشان داده شده - حد ضرر درست زیر کف آخرین کندل 30 دقیقه‌ایِ عبورکننده از خط IQM تایم‌فریم بالاتر (افقی سیاه) و IQM تایم‌فریم پایین (خط قرمز توپر) قرار دارد. یادداشت‌های روی نمودار مسئلهٔ گذاشتن سفارش ورودم در بالای مستطیل سایه‌زنی زرد را تکرار می‌کنند.

تارگت (و ورود) در این مرحله هنوز قطعی نیستند - دلیلش این است که نمی‌توانم ورودم را بگذارم مگر اینکه مطمئن باشم تارگتم کجاست، و تا وقتی PA بیشتری را در حال شکل‌گیری نبینم دربارهٔ محل تارگتم راحت نیستم. مخصوصاً، می‌خواهم PA را ببینم تا وقتی به ورودم نزدیک می‌شود. در این مرحله، شکست نزولی آیندهٔ «FL»ای که روی نمودار پایین برچسب‌گذاری شده را به‌عنوان محتمل‌ترین ناحیه‌ای می‌بینم که پوزیشن لانگم با مجموعهٔ قابل‌توجه سفارش‌های فروش روبه‌رو می‌شود که می‌تواند قیمت را پایین‌تر برگرداند. بسته به اینکه PA چطور تا وقتی قیمت به ورودم نزدیک می‌شود شکل می‌گیرد، تارگت ممکن است کوتاه‌تر شود. اگر آره، ورودم هم احتمالاً پایین‌تر تنظیم می‌شود - برای کم کردن ریسک بین ورودم و حد ضرر. سفارش ورود فعلی‌ام در ناحیه‌ای گذاشته شده که حد ضرر 14 پیپی می‌خواهد. این برای من حد ضرر بالایی است - معمولاً دوست دارم حد ضرر‌ام 10 پیپ یا کمتر باشد. الزام تارگتم حداقل 3 برابر ریسک است. در این مورد، تارگت تقریباً 64 پیپ از ورود دور است (حدود 4.5 R). اگر تارگتم پایین‌تر بیاید، ورودم هم متناسب پایین می‌آید. حد ضرر‌ام عوض نمی‌شود.

یادداشت سریع دربارهٔ روش‌شناسی ورودم (هنوز در حال پالایش رویکرد استانداردم برای گذاشتن سفارش ورود هستم): می‌فهمم که قیمت ممکن است قبل از رسیدن به ورودم برگردد - در واقع، این به‌طور منظم اتفاق می‌افتد. تصمیم گرفته‌ام فرصت‌های معاملاتی خوب را برای یک برنامهٔ مدیریت ریسک سخت فدا کنم. با جاماندن از معاملات مشکلی ندارم اما با ریسک زیاد کردن مشکلی دارم. سال‌ها پیش یک حساب لایو خیلی بزرگ را در عرض چند ماه کوتاه از دست دادم. این دیگر هرگز اتفاق نمی‌افتد. دلیل اصلی اینکه به‌جای تنظیم ورود برای کنترل ریسک، اندازهٔ پوزیشنم را تنظیم نمی‌کنم، مسئلهٔ تارگتم است - حد ضرر‌های پهن تارگت به همان اندازه پهنی می‌خواهند تا الزام ریسک/بازدهٔ 3X من را برآورده کنند. تخصص اصلی من اجرای معاملات کم‌ریسک کوتاه‌مدت 'فرصت' خواهد بود. وقتی SL از 10 پیپ بیشتر شود، الزام تارگتم از 30-40 پیپ بیشتر می‌شود و معامله طولانی‌تر طول می‌کشد، که معامله‌ام را در معرض ریسک خارجی بیشتر قرار می‌دهد.

I want to share some insights I've been working on recently regarding trading around a FO.

We all know why a FO is an ideal place to look for a bounce. Not ever FO will react nicely however, and after many hours of simulated trading I am beginning to see certain patterns that drastically increase the likelihood of a bounce. In my opinion, knowing if price will bounce at a a FO level depends mainly on the PA to the left of the FO itself. The best FO bounces occur when price forms a FO after establishing a range, between two FL's (upper and lower FL).

In the case of my trade below, the upper FL is formed as the result of an engulf of a Flag to its left.. this is important, and it makes the future FO of this FL very important. Once the correct FL is identified and faked out, the rest is super easy. In this case, I knew I had a runner because of the engulf in to compression below, with price missing the main demand zone by just a few pips. Price forms a deep RT to gather enough bearish LQ to fuel the move down. They have to shake loose all sellers first, so they have ample LQ to sell in to. The result is a whole lot of trapped buyers...and plenty of LQ for the push down.

I know everyone here is aware of this kind of setup.. I am not discussing anything new...but many failed trades (as I see in my trading and other's trading) is the result of picking a weak LS/starting point. In the case of this EU trade below, the starting point was the FL that formed after price broke out of Box 1. That new FL is labeled as FL "A", and it is highly significant because it is the FL that contains the range where price faked out to the upside. When price returns to the important decision points, the entry is easy, the SL is easy, and the target is the demand zone below where price engulfed in to compression.

Hope these are some useful thoughts to ponder

همه می‌دانیم چرا FO جای ایده‌آلی برای جست‌وجوی برگشت است. با این حال، هر FO واکنش خوبی نمی‌دهد و بعد از ساعت‌های زیادی معاملهٔ شبیه‌سازی، شروع می‌کنم به دیدن الگوهای مشخصی که احتمال برگشت را به‌طور چشمگیری افزایش می‌دهند. به نظر من، دانستن اینکه آیا قیمت روی یک سطح FO برمی‌گردد یا نه، عمدتاً به PA در چپ خود FO بستگی دارد. بهترین برگشت‌های FO وقتی رخ می‌دهند که قیمت بعد از شکل‌گیری یک رنج، بین دو FL (FL بالایی و FL پایینی) FO می‌کند.

در مورد معاملهٔ پایینم، FL بالایی در نتیجهٔ اینگالف یک Flag در چپش شکل گرفته… این مهم است و FO آیندهٔ این FL را خیلی مهم می‌کند. وقتی FL درست شناسایی و فیک‌اوت شد، بقیه فوق‌العاده آسان است. در این مورد، می‌دانستم معامله‌گر برنده‌ای دارم به خاطر اینگالف به فشردگی پایین، با قیمتی که فقط چند پیپ از ناحیهٔ اصلی تقاضا جا مانده بود. قیمت RT عمیقی می‌کند تا LQ نزولی کافی برای حرکت به پایین جمع کند. اول باید همهٔ فروشندگان را تکان بدهند تا LQ فراوانی برای فروش به آن‌ها داشته باشند. نتیجه تعداد زیادی خریدار به‌دام‌افتاده است… و LQ فراوان برای هل دادن به پایین.

می‌دانم همهٔ این‌جا از این‌نوع ستاپ آگاه‌اند… من چیز جدیدی بحث نمی‌کنم… اما بسیاری از معاملات شکست‌خورده (همان‌طور که در معاملهٔ خودم و دیگران می‌بینم) نتیجهٔ انتخاب LS ضعیف/نقطهٔ شروع ضعیف است. در مورد این معاملهٔ EU پایین، نقطهٔ شروع FL‌ای بود که بعد از شکست قیمت از Box 1 شکل گرفت. آن FL جدید با FL «A» برچسب‌گذاری شده و خیلی مهم است چون FL‌ای است که رنجی را شامل می‌شود که قیمت در آن به سمت بالا فیک‌اوت کرد. وقتی قیمت به نقاط تصمیم‌گیری مهم برمی‌گردد، ورود آسان است، SL آسان است و تارگت ناحیهٔ تقاضای پایین است که قیمت در آن به فشردگی اینگالف کرد.

امیدوارم این نکته‌ها برای فکر کردن مفید باشند

The hard part of trading these FO bounces is knowing where price will bounce when the kink is wide. The wider the kink, the higher the risk. The best way to refine an entry when a kink is wide, is looking for a LTF 'inner kink'. Often times, price will bounce from the inner kink, inside of the larger scale kink. This is a big part of understanding how to use scale to your advantage.

In the case of the simulation below, there was no inner kink because my charting package only goes to 1-min candles and there was not enough detail. In this case, I drew the mouth of the kink & waited for a reaction there. But...here is where it gets tricky. When I trade, I want very little draw down. I usually like to keep my SL at or below 15 pips. If I had waited to short price deeper in the FL Box (as opposed to shorting the mouth), I would have been stopped out. The first two touches of the mouth took all of the short orders, leaving plenty of room for buyers to break through and establish control & a new high.

The rule I am currently working with when it comes to these setups:

1. If the setup is too confusing, just skip it and look for something else. If it doesn't 'jump out' at me right away, I look for a different trade.

2. If I want to trade it however, I will look to trade the mouth first, with a tight SL. (this is assuming the kink is wide and there is not inner kink to use as reference).

3. Each FO is a RBD or a DBR. In the chart below, the FO was a RBD. Look where the "drop" is... you can see that is a base. When price reacts to the mouth of the kink, it RT to the base. To me, that is a sign that price is ready to move higher. It did not engulf that base to the downside... i would be very cautious shorting a 3rd visit deeper in to the blue FL box.

These are the details that make or break a trade. It gets hard, because the intricacies of trading are somewhat subjective and it is almost impossible to teach this. I'm sure there is a better way to trade these setups, but this is my current take on it.

در مورد شبیه‌سازی پایین، چون پکیج نموداری‌ام فقط تا کندل 1 دقیقه‌ای می‌رفت و جزئیات کافی نبود، kink داخلی نبود. در این مورد، دهانهٔ kink را کشیدم و منتظر واکنش آن‌جا بودم. اما… این‌جاست که پیچیده می‌شود. وقتی معامله می‌کنم، drawdown خیلی کمی می‌خواهم. معمولاً دوست دارم SL‌ام 15 پیپ یا کمتر باشد. اگر منتظر می‌ماندم قیمت را عمیق‌تر در FL Box فروش کنم (به‌جای فروش دهانه)، استاپ می‌شدم. دو لمسهٔ اول دهانه همهٔ سفارش‌های فروش را گرفت و جای فراوانی برای خریداران گذاشت تا بشکنند و کنترل را به دست بگیرند و سقف جدید بسازند.

قانونی که الان برای این‌نوع ستاپ‌ها با آن کار می‌کنم:

1. اگر ستاپ خیلی گیج‌کننده بود، ردش کن و دنبال چیز دیگری بگرد. اگر فوراً به چشمم نپرد، به دنبال معاملهٔ دیگری می‌گردم.

2. اگر با این حال بخواهم معامله‌اش کنم، اول دهانه را با SL تنگ معامله می‌کنم. (این با فرض این است که kink پهن است و kink داخلی برای مرجع نیست).

3. هر FO یک RBD یا DBR است. روی نمودار پایین، FO یک RBD بود. نگاه کن «سقوط» کجاست… می‌بینی یک پایه است. وقتی قیمت به دهانهٔ kink واکنش نشان می‌دهد، به همان پایه RT می‌کند. برای من، این نشانه‌ای است که قیمت آمادهٔ حرکت بالاتر است. آن پایه را به سمت پایین اینگالف نکرد… در فروش کردن سومین بازدیدِ عمیق‌تر داخل جعبهٔ FL آبی خیلی محتاط می‌شدم.

این‌ها جزئیاتی هستند که معامله را می‌سازند یا می‌شکنند. سخت می‌شود، چون ظرافت‌های معامله تا حدی ذهنی‌اند و تدریسشان تقریباً غیرممکن است. مطمئنم راه بهتری برای معاملهٔ این‌نوع ستاپ‌ها هست، اما این دید فعلی من است.

My answer: looking left, I can see a clear trick occurring. He sets up the buy side trade after price RT to the old FO zone (looking left). Here is a HTF chart showing the exact area where price reacted. I don't think this was a coincidence. That FL is the lightly grey shaded box. This entire analysis seems to be anchored in the ignoring of a QM level and FO to the left.

A couple important things to point out:

You can see that FL box by looking at the first chart I posted on this EU example... it is the basis of his FL Box analysis.

In reference to my post # 1937:

It is always hard to decide whether a lost trade is simply a fluke of the market (which happens) or if it was an error on my part. Post # 1937 is a perfect example. At first, I wrote it off as a 'fluke'. but after seeing the perfect reaction on the EA trade on post # 1938, I think I am still missing a piece of critical analysis.

My hunch is that the 'missing piece' has everything to do with the relationship between a swap zone & a FO. It is important to see where the FO occurs... I remember Salivan mentioning something about looking for a FO that occurs in to another FL. He might mean that the FO needs to dip through the FL in to the opposite swap zone to clear out all residual LQ.

If you refer back to my EUR-AUD trade on Post # 1938, you will see a great entry point with very little DD. If you look to the left of my entry, you will see a clear FO that occurs below the distal edge of the black box. That FO and subsequent high is drawn using the blue box. I am pretty sure the false move to the downside (in to a PAZ below) is key in getting the right bounce when price returns for the FOF that remains at that level.

My apologies if I am doing a bad job of explaining this... there concepts are notoriously difficult to describe using words

But for those who are struggling....start looking left and spend more time understanding what price is doing as it forms prior to the main FL where you start looking for an entry. Left side data is crucial, and I am still learning how to read it properly.

Confluence of the following factors is important as well:

1. Swap Zone

2. FO/False moves 3. Clean orders 4. Squaring up 5. Drawing FL Boxes & decisions in the right FL to prepare for an entry 6. ** False supply/demand zones that set up just above/below true supply or true demand. 5. Opposing targets (aka opposing tricks)

This is what I will continue working on.

Here is a simple version of the EA trade that worked out well in my post above.

If you look at the chart below, you will see I labeled FL "A" for reference. There is a tiny LTF kink that forms after price breaks the top of FL "A", but price forms a FO below that kink as well. The FO drops all the way back in to FL "A" (imagine if I extended FL "A" all the way to the right...). I think this holds importance because it is clearing residual LQ, making it much more likely that price will bounce bullish when price RT to the yellow box I drew.

We always want to make sure the last pocket of short orders is taken if we are looking to get long, otherwise, price is likely to do whatever is necessary to absorb that LQ. Clearing the last pocket of sell orders loads the buyers, and we can proceed to mark up the correct FL to find where the opposite orders are executed and FOF is created.

حدسم این است که «تکهٔ گمشده» همه‌چیزش به رابطهٔ بین ناحیهٔ سواپ و FO مربوط است. دیدن این‌که FO کجا رخ می‌دهد مهم است… یادم می‌آید Salivan دربارهٔ جست‌وجوی FO‌ای که وارد یک FL دیگر می‌شود حرفی زد. شاید منظورش این بود که FO باید از FL عبور کند و وارد ناحیهٔ سواپ مخالف شود تا همهٔ LQ باقی‌مانده را پاک کند.

اگر به معاملهٔ EUR-AUD من در پست # 1938 برگردید، یک نقطهٔ ورود عالی با DD بسیار کم می‌بینید. اگر به سمت چپ ورودم نگاه کنید، یک FO واضح می‌بینید که زیر لبهٔ دور کادر سیاه رخ می‌دهد. آن FO و سقف بعدی با کادر آبی کشیده شده‌اند. تقریباً مطمئنم حرکت کاذب به سمت پایین (به داخل یک PAZ پایین‌تر) کلیدِ گرفتن جهش درست است وقتی قیمت برای FOF‌ای که در همان سطح باقی مانده برمی‌گردد.

اگر در توضیح این خوب عمل نمی‌کنم ببخشید… توصیف این مفاهیم با کلمات بدنامانه دشوار است

اما برای کسانی که گیر کرده‌اند… شروع کنید به نگاه‌کردن به چپ و زمان بیشتری برای فهمیدن این‌که قیمت هنگام شکل‌گرفتنش پیش از FL اصلی که شروع به جست‌وجوی ورود در آن می‌کنید چه می‌کند بگذارید. دادهٔ سمت چپ حیاتی است و من هنوز دارم یاد می‌گیرم آن را درست بخوانم.

تلاقی عوامل زیر هم مهم است:

1. ناحیهٔ سواپ

2. FO/حرکت‌های کاذب 3. سفارش‌های تمیز 4. Square up (تسویهٔ سفارش‌ها) 5. کشیدن کادرهای FL و تصمیم‌گیری در FL درست برای آماده‌شدن برای ورود 6. ** ناحیه‌های عرضه/تقاضای کاذب که درست بالای/زیر عرضه یا تقاضای واقعی شکل می‌گیرند. 5. تارگت‌های مخالف (همان تریک‌های مخالف)

این همان چیزی است که به کار روی آن ادامه می‌دهم.

اینجا نسخهٔ ساده‌ای از معاملهٔ EA است که در پست بالا خوب پیش رفت.

اگر به چارت پایین نگاه کنید، می‌بینید که FL را برای ارجاع «A» نام‌گذاری کردم. یک kink کوچک در LTF درست بعد از این‌که قیمت بالای FL «A» را شکست شکل می‌گیرد، ولی قیمت زیر آن kink هم یک FO می‌سازد. FO همه‌راه تا داخل FL «A» برمی‌گردد (تصور کنید اگر FL «A» را همه‌راه تا راست امتداد می‌دادم… ). فکر می‌کنم این اهمیت دارد چون LQ باقی‌مانده را پاک می‌کند و احتمال جهش صعودی قیمت را وقتی به کادر زردی که کشیدم RT می‌کند خیلی بیشتر می‌کند.

همیشه می‌خواهیم مطمئن شویم آخرین گروه سفارش‌های فروش گرفته شده است اگر دنبال خرید هستیم، در غیر این صورت قیمت احتمالاً هر کاری لازم باشد برای جذب آن LQ می‌کند. پاک‌کردن آخرین گروه سفارش‌های فروش خریداران را بارگیری می‌کند و می‌توانیم ادامه دهیم و FL درست را علامت بزنیم تا بفهمیم سفارش‌های مخالف کجا اجرا می‌شوند و FOF ساخته می‌شود.

This way of looking at the market is still pretty new to me.. but I am looking specifically for a swap zone to start the analysis. The swap zone has to include a FL that holds price up, and a FL that holds price down (I think the terminology is LFL and UFL). If drawn correctly, this should create space between these FL's. It is in this 'space' that I want to see a FO occur.

I mark all of these zones as they form...then I start looking closer to see if there is an opportunity to make a trade. I treat each UFL/LFL combination as a 'system'.

Here is a drawing:

There isn't always space between the FL's, but if there is not space, then there is always an overlap. Here is a drawing that shows overlap, but no 'open space'.

I haven't done enough testing to find out which scenario is better, but so far, I prefer the situation where there is space between the two (usually you can see a very LTF kink in the space). The key is the FO... I want to see 'clean orders' in the form of a false move to trap LQ on the wrong side. It is the FO that occurs between the two FL's that form the swap zone that seems to clear out all residual LQ..making a bounce trade perfect.

If the FO forms and clean orders are left behind, I can trade along side the IT's when they square up their positions. It is the 'squaring up' that causes the bounce.

There are some exceptions to this.. most notably situations that incorporate compression. Compression creates atypical PA and usually I set my order just at the beginning of compression (or at the very least I will place my stop beyond the compression area). When I get stopped out using this method it is almost always because I misread compression.

Looking at your example on AUD-USD, I didn't quite see the swap zone. I do see your methodology however, and I think you are on the right track.

I formulated this way of looking at the market after revisiting Salivan's trades... he regularly took trades at the last possible pocket of supply/demand near a swap zone. It almost always happened near a FO/trick. I am curious if other traders see the same opportunity as I do!

این روش نگاه‌کردن به بازار هنوز برایم نسبتاً تازه است… ولی من به‌طور خاص دنبال یک ناحیهٔ سواپ برای شروع تحلیل هستم. ناحیهٔ سواپ باید شامل یک FL باشد که قیمت را بالا نگه می‌دارد و یک FL که قیمت را پایین نگه می‌دارد (فکر می‌کنم اصطلاحش LFL و UFL است). اگر درست کشیده شود، باید بین این FL‌ها فاصله ایجاد کند. در همین «فاصله» است که می‌خواهم FO رخ بدهد را ببینم.

همهٔ این ناحیه‌ها را همان‌طور که شکل می‌گیرند علامت می‌زنم… بعد دقیق‌تر نگاه می‌کنم ببینم فرصتی برای معامله هست یا نه. هر ترکیب UFL/LFL را یک «سیستم» می‌دانم.

اینجا یک نگاشت است:

همیشه بین FL‌ها فاصله نیست، ولی اگر فاصله نباشد، همیشه هم‌پوشانی هست. اینجا نگاشت‌ای می‌بینید که هم‌پوشانی را نشان می‌دهد، ولی «فضای باز» نیست.

هنوز تست کافی انجام نداده‌ام که بفهمم کدام سناریو بهتر است، ولی تا حالا حالتی را ترجیح می‌دهم که بین این دو فاصله باشد (معمولاً می‌توان یک kink بسیار LTF در آن فاصله دید). کلید FO است… می‌خواهم «سفارش‌های تمیز» را در قالب یک حرکت کاذب ببینم که LQ را در سمت اشتباه به دام می‌اندازد. FO‌ای که بین دو FL‌ای که ناحیهٔ سواپ را می‌سازند رخ می‌دهد به‌نظر می‌رسد همهٔ LQ باقی‌مانده را پاک می‌کند… که معاملهٔ جهش را کامل می‌کند.

اگر FO شکل بگیرد و سفارش‌های تمیز پشت سر بمانند، می‌توانم هم‌زمان با IT‌ها معامله کنم وقتی موقعیت‌هایشان را square up می‌کنند. همان square up است که باعث جهش می‌شود.

چند استثنا برای این هست… به‌خصوص موقعیت‌هایی که فشردگی دارند. فشردگی PA غیرمعمول می‌سازد و معمولاً سفارتم را دقیقاً ابتدای فشردگی می‌گذارم (یا دست‌کم استاپم را آن‌ورای ناحیهٔ فشردگی می‌گذارم). وقتی با این روش استاپ می‌شوم تقریباً همیشه به‌خاطر این است که فشردگی را اشتباه خوانده‌ام.

با نگاه به مثال تو روی AUD-USD، ناحیهٔ سواپ را کامل ندیدم. با این حال روش تو را می‌بینم و فکر می‌کنم در مسیر درستی هستی.

Hi GGJJ,

Not entirely sure if I am correct, but the way I understand the 'last pocket of orders' is being the last place where buyers/seller took control of the market. There are two important pieces of information:

1. The decision to FO 2. the FTR/FL that forms after the engulf of the decision to FO.

The FTR/FL that forms after the engulf of the decision to FO is the last place where sell orders took control of the market, following the FO. When price returns to that last pocket of LQ, price bounces. That is also where price returns to 'square up' after the trick occurs ($$$ is spent to move the market in the wrong direction, and those who invest in this false move need to eventually exit their position, as it remains a constant drag on their balance sheet until the position is closed.

This is my understanding of why this 'last pocket' of LQ is so important.

Here is a basic drawing:

Specifically for the AUD-USD trade, the decision to FO is drawn, and the engulf of the Decision to FO is also drawn. That FTR/FL is where I took the trade. In my opinion, the 'last pocket' is the FL labeled 'X" below. Technically, you could have chosen the first red box, or either of the purple boxes as the 'decision to FO' and you would still end up with the same FL "X". It is in the FL "X" that price bounces.

Something I noticed about that USD-CAD Short:

There were two scales involved with this trade. The First scale has a UFL and LFL and FO, and the lower scale has the same structure: UFL, LFL, and FO. The reasons I call it the "second scale" is because it forms as a result of it's reaction to the first scale.

What ends up forming, are two FO's.

Not sure how useful this is in trading these zones, but it might be a good idea to find multiple scale FO's occurring in close proximity together, because it decreases the likelihood that price will FO above your entry (If the space above your entry is just a higher TF scale with its own FO).

Great entry, but I still got stopped out on this EUR-USD Simulation.

It's a good reminder to be reasonable about targets. In this case, I kept my SL very tight, but my target was too wide. If I widened my SL to just above the FO, my original TG would have been hit nicely.

My Lesson:

If you take a trade with a very tight SL, make sure your target is reasonable (specifically, make sure your TG is placed at the first possible place where price might encounter resistance.). If you want a wider target, keep in mind that your SL may need to be widened to give price a little breathing room.

Reasons why this FO did not work:

1. The FL that price Fakes out was not formed as the result of an engulf of something important

2. Price did not make lower lows prior to the FO occurring, which means fewer sellers would be committing to the short. which means fewer traders panic and go long when the see the bullish FO.

1. FL‌ای که قیمت از آن فیک‌اوت کرد در نتیجهٔ اینگالفِ چیز مهمی شکل نگرفته بود

2. قیمت پیش از رخدادن FO کف‌های پایین‌تر نساخت، یعنی فروشندگان کمتری به فروش متعهد می‌شوند. یعنی تریدرهای کمتری وقتی FO صعودی را می‌بینند وحشت می‌کنند و خرید می‌شوند.

Something I noticed about that USD-CAD Short:

There were two scales involved with this trade. The First scale has a UFL and LFL and FO, and the lower scale has the same structure: UFL, LFL, and FO. The reasons I call it the "second scale" is because it forms as a result of it's reaction to the first scale.

This one started on Aug 1st.

The reason for taking a long was the FO shown at the bottom of the screen in the red circle.

I will start with the 30-min chart showing the entry and both targets. The 1st target was relatively straightforward, but the reason for staying in the trade after closing a portion of the position was the engulf located in the yellow circle... the target of that engulf gave me the 2nd Target of my buy trade @ the MPL. The MPL area of that FL is shown by the green rectangular box at the top of the screen. I exited the trade just before that MPL area (in case price bounced from a LTF "mouth" kink instead of making it all of the way into the MPL itself).

The next chart shows a detailed view of my entry on a LTF 1-minute chart. My exact entry was at the LTF QM level of the UFL formed after price engulfed the LFL. In this case, since I don't have data below a 1-minute chart, I had to use the entire 1-min candle as my LFL. While not shown on this chart, my SL was placed directly below the the fakeout itself. The SL was located 6 pips from my entry point.

The hourly chart below shows the reason I noticed this area to begin with. Basically, saw several consecutive lower lows, with one big move up just prior to the final lower low push. I saw this as an excellent bear trap. Specifically, I see that everyone starts buying at Point # 1 after several lower lows and higher lows. Traders see this as the end of the downward trend and start buying. Shorty thereafter, price cannot sustain this bullish push and price crashes down scaring everyone who got long and catching all of their stops at Point # 2. When Low # 4 forms, breakout traders get short and everyone who was long has closed out their positions and are looking to go short. Bearish traders are placing their stop losses above.

If you look at the green flag limit I drew, you can see Point # 3 is a FO below the box. This is the exact location of the trick. It is in this location where I will be looking to Buy (on a lower TF) when price returns.Those who were short at the FO are caught when price snaps back up. No major dips back in to this zone, so clean orders are formed at Point # 4 (they don't have a chance to get out in time). IT's have short orders trapped here as well. They have to square up eventually, and when they come back, I will be waiting. Eventually, price does return and I buy at Point # 5.

Hope this helps share my process!

دلیل گرفتن خرید همان FO بود که در دایرهٔ قرمز پایین صفحه نشان داده شده.

اینجا چارت 30-min را می‌بینید که ورود و هر دو تارگت را نشان می‌دهد. تارگت اول نسبتاً سرراست بود، ولی دلیل ماندن در معامله بعد از بستن بخشی از موقعیت، اینگالفی بود که در دایرهٔ زرد قرار داشت… تارگت آن اینگالف تارگت دوم معاملهٔ خرید من را در MPL داد. ناحیهٔ MPL آن FL با کادر مستطیلی سبز در بالای صفحه نشان داده شده. از معامله دقیقاً پیش از آن ناحیهٔ MPL خارج شدم (در صورت این‌که قیمت از kink «دهانهٔ» LTF جهش کند به‌جای این‌که تا خود MPL برسد).

چارت بعدی نمای دقیقی از ورودم روی چارت 1-min تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر را نشان می‌دهد. ورود دقیق من در سطح QM تایم‌فریم پایین‌ترِ UFL بود که بعد از اینگالفِ قیمتِ LFL شکل گرفت. در این حالت، چون داده‌ای پایین‌تر از چارت 1-min ندارم، مجبور شدم کل کندل 1-min را به‌عنوان LFL خودم استفاده کنم. اگرچه در این چارت نشان داده نشده، SL من دقیقاً زیر خود فیک‌اوت گذاشته شده بود. SL شش پیپ از نقطهٔ ورودم فاصله داشت.

چارت ساعتی پایین دلیل متوجه‌شدن من از این ناحیه از اول را نشان می‌دهد. اساساً، چند کف پایین‌تر پی‌درپی را دیدم، با یک حرکت بزرگ به بالا درست پیش از فشار کف پایین‌تر نهایی. این را تلهٔ خرسی عالی دیدم. به‌طور خاص می‌بینم همه بعد از چند کف پایین‌تر و کف‌های بالاتر در نقطهٔ # 1 شروع به خریدن می‌کنند. معامله‌گران این را پایان روند نزولی می‌بینند و شروع به خرید می‌کنند. کمی بعد، قیمت نمی‌تواند این فشار صعودی را نگه دارد و قیمت با ترساندن همهٔ خرید‌ها سقوط می‌کند و استاپ‌های همه را در نقطهٔ # 2 می‌گیرد. وقتی کف # 4 شکل می‌گیرد، تریدرهای شکست فروش می‌شوند و همهٔ خرید‌ها موقعیت‌هایشان را بسته‌اند و دنبال فروش هستند. تریدرهای نزولی حد ضرر‌هایشان را بالای آن می‌گذارند.

اگر به فلگ لیمیت سبزی که کشیدم نگاه کنی، می‌بینی نقطهٔ # 3 یک FO زیر کادر است. این دقیقاً جای تریک است. در همین جاست که وقتی قیمت برمی‌گردد در تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر دنبال خرید خواهم بود. کسانی که در FO فروش بودند وقتی قیمت سریع برمی‌گردد گیر می‌افتند. هیچ ریزش بزرگی به داخل این ناحیه نمی‌شود، پس سفارش‌های تمیز در نقطهٔ # 4 شکل می‌گیرند (فرصتی برای خروج به‌موقع ندارند). IT‌ها هم سفارش‌های فروش در این‌جا به دام افتاده‌اند. در نهایت باید square up کنند و وقتی برمی‌گردند، من منتظر خواهم بود. در نهایت قیمت برمی‌گردد و در نقطهٔ # 5 می‌خرم.

The reason I drew my box instead of your box: the engulf of your box pretty much hit its target immediately...it was of no use to me. It wasn't until price engulfed out of that LTF FL (my box) that I had an engulf with an unmet target.

So, in summary, I chose the FL who's engulf pushed price in to a pole, with an unmet target above. You could sum it up in one word: Scale.

Second Reason: Proximity to LTF trick above:

Salivan had a concept which he referred to as 'magnetic attraction' as it referred to to price being attracted to certain areas of the chart based on the LQ that exists at that particular level. In my experience, price is attracted to areas where previous fakeouts have happened... and we know the best FO's are the ones that leave no room for trapped traders to get out in time.. simply put, the best FO's are proceeded with a sharp move away (pole). In this case, there was a mini trick, and price shot away very quickly, forming a pole in its wake.

If you keep the chart on the this TF, you can see price shot down quickly and didn't hesitate until it formed the first FL/FTR (this is my box). It was the first time price stopped to "catch its breath" after a trick and sharp pole-down. So, this FL/FTR is important to me. When my box bounces price and a new low is formed (the formation of your box), I give even more weight to my box. It is the "final northern frontier" before getting back on that 'highway' that leads directly back to the trick above. It is the last stop before that 'magnetc attraction' starts pulling price back in.

Hope this is at least a little useful to you. I hate ambiguity, so I try to make sure my answers are as direct as possible.

If anyone disagrees with me, please feel free to say so! I am wrong all the time.

Here is a recent drawing I made to explain my updated strategy for trading price's RT to a previous FO.

Something interesting I just thought of: the FO of the LFL in the drawing and subsequent low confirms the original LFL as an "inner FL" or "inner kink".

This ties in nicely with what I was practicing yesterday when I said price engulfs, then forms FO

If applied to this drawing, the LFL or "inner kink" is also and engulf, which precedes the FO.

The tricky part is verifying that the "engulf" has a valid unmet target. If so, you are clear to trade price's RT to the FO that forms as part of the 'outer kink'. But, if the target of the engulf (inner kink) is already met, the "FO" of the inner kink is actually an engulf. Why? Because price has no reason to FO if price is coming from a met target. Any breach of a level (if price is coming from a met target) is indicative of future price direction (it's not a trick; it's an engulf). When price is coming from an unmet target the breached levels are FO's...tricks are needed because there is an unmet target. If you miss this detail, the trade will fail. This is a new concept for me, so please don't accept this as being 100% accurate....but it's certainly worth thinking about.

معامله سخت و زمان‌بر است… باید همیشه روی پیدا کردن راه‌هایی برای ساده‌ترکردنش تمرکز کنیم… تا وقتی نظم و روش‌شناسی اصلی‌مان را قربانی نکنیم.

به نظرم نیمی از نبرد برای سودده‌بودن به‌عنوان معامله‌گر فهمیدن این است که دنبال چه بگردی… ولی نیمهٔ دیگر توانایی پیداکردنش وقتی بازار زنده است و اجرای درست معامله با تمرکز ذهنی درست است. از دست‌دادن ستاپ‌ها آسان است… مدیریت وقت حیاتی است. همچنین مهم است روشی کارآمد برای کشیدن چارت‌ها و ردیابی PA هنگام بازشدن در لحظه توسعه بدهی.

I want to refer back to a trade call I made last week on EUR-AUD (You can see it on my post # 2096).

I am detailing this trade because it is a setup that works almost all of the time...with tremendous reliability. The hard part is understanding the methodology and having the ability to apply it properly to a live chart.

Please feel free to challenge me if I say anything incorrect

First, here is a copied chart from post # 2096:

But here is more detail as to why I took this trade:

Take a look at point # 1 and point # 2: they are both fakeouts. The important part of trading these accurately is taking the time to carefully analyze where the perspective FO forms. I have a bad tendency to get sloppy when it comes to carefully analyzing the exact location of the FO. This is the reason for many of my losing trades (I went through a bunch of losing trades from 2017 this year and noticed many losses happen as a result of sloppy mistakes on my end).

It starts with drawing FL Boxes at the right locations: in close proximity to swap zones. Once the boxes are carefully drawn, it is much easier to see how price reacts to them. But it's not always clear.

In this example, look at FO # 1. Despite missing my main FL Boxes, FO # 1 ends up forming at a very important area: pre compression. Price came just shy of engulfing in to compression. This makes FO # 1 important. Not all valid FO's will bounce price because they aren't created equal...all FO's have varying degrees of strength. Pre-compression is one of the strongest.

When price forms FO # 2 you can see price does not engulf any LTF FL's...and once again there is an important FO. The rest is easy...finding that exact entry becomes pretty simple once the FO's are drawn and verified as being strong. Specifically, I extended the red 'inner kink' over to the right and used that as my detailed entry point (since it is located within a larger HTF kink). Look how perfectly price respected that red inner kink.

با کشیدن کادرهای FL تو جای درست شروع می‌شه: نزدیک نواحی سواپ. وقتی کادرها با دقت کشیده بشن، دیدن واکنش قیمت بهشون خیلی راحت‌تره. ولی همیشه این‌طور نیست.

وقتی قیمت FO # 2 رو می‌سازه می‌بینی قیمت هیچ FL‌ای از LTF رو اینگالف نمی‌کنه… و باز هم یه FO مهم هست. بقیه‌ش آسونه… پیدا کردن اون ورود دقیق وقتی FO‌ها کشیده و تأیید بشن که قوی‌ان نسبتاً ساده می‌شه. به‌طور خاص، کینک داخلی قرمز رو به راست امتداد دادم و ازش به‌عنوان نقطهٔ ورود دقیق خودم استفاده کردم (چون داخل یه کینک بزرگ‌تر HTF قرار داره). ببین قیمت چقدر تمیز به اون کینک داخلی قرمز واکنش نشون داد.

Hi Pinkpanter,

You have some good questions...I might be the wrong person to ask when it comes to kinks and engulfs.

Lately, I have been focusing my attention on trading the return to an important fakeout. Ideally, there will be two fakeouts happening- each in their own scale.

I want a high time frame fakeout, followed by a slightly lower scale FO... then I trade the RT to the that smaller FO. A good example of this is in Post # 2127 above.

You can see I went short on EU at the second FO. These FO were on the same scale, but it still looked good because FO # 1 did not engulf anything important on the LTF. This is why I felt comfortable shorting at the second FO.

Also, and maybe most importantly, I need to see a valid FO AND clean orders to take a trade.

To me: Clean orders = trapped traders = LQ waiting on price's RT

If I was looking at your chart, and I had no other TF to look at, this is how I would analyze it:

I would look at the area I marked FO # 1 on LTF to see exactly what it was reacting to. Was there an engulf on LTF? If so, avoid a trade on FO 2. I am not impressed by FO #1...there isn't much of a FO happening here, although it does happen near a swap zone, so it is worth looking at on LTF. The FO has to occur in to an important area without engulfing.

If there is no EG on FO #1, then FO 2 is possibly in play...but there must be clean orders (trapped traders with LQ) at the FO # 2 area. From what I see on this chart, there are not any clean orders..price meandered away. No trap means I am not trading it. I would look at a new chart.

But don't be discouraged

... I am working on a very specific type of strategy. There

are countless ways to apply RTM theory and add your own strategic influence to specialize in a specific type of setup.

Maybe someone else can do a better job of answering your question. I hope my response was somewhat useful!

Hi GGJJ,

It is always hard to find the place where price will bounce once you find the right FO to trade from. Usually, I look for that last FL or decision point before price fakes out....but I also look at that potential entry point in relation to the size of the FO and the FL Boxes around it to see (visually) if my entry is reasonable. I always ask: Is my entry too far below the place where the FO eventually stops? If so, the risk is pretty high and I may adjust my entry.

I wish I had a concrete answer for exactly how to find the perfect entry every time... but the closest I can get to that is:

Use the last FTR/FL that formed before the FO occurs...you want the last place where price hesitated before shooting up (or down) to form the FO You want the place right before the trick happened...where all the traders got stopped and BO traders got in on the wrong side. Here is a diagram to show how I incorporate trapped/clean orders with the QM setup. The "HH" (or head) of the QM forming should itself be a reaction to clean orders below it. Once this happens, the LQ left behind by the trapped orders is taken, and the shoulder of that QM is the last pocket of orders remaining.

I saw this happen on UJ perfectly.

This is just a way of tracking where the LQ is likely to be existing so you can position yourself to trade the bounce.

اینجا دیاگرامی هست که نشون می‌ده چطور سفارش‌های به‌دام‌افتاده/تمیز رو با ستاپ QM ترکیب می‌کنم. «HH» (یا سر) QM شکل‌گرفته باید خودش واکنشی به سفارش‌های تمیزِ زیرش باشه. وقتی این اتفاق می‌افته، LQ‌ای که سفارش‌های به‌دام‌افتاده پشت سر می‌ذارن گرفته می‌شه و شانهٔ اون QM آخرین گروه سفارش‌های باقی‌مونده‌ست.

I think the general concept is remaining LQ is left over from trapped orders occurring when price fakes out before turning abruptly. All this type of trade is: taking advantage of the 'bounce' from left over orders at a level where there was some previous carnage.

The stronger the false move, and the stronger the move away from that false move, the greater likelihood of a a bounce when price returns to that area.

Also, the false move should break highs or lows to its left (it should be convincing.. because the more convincing the false move, the more trapped LQ remaining at that level.

I am going to keep back testing this to see how frequently we get at least a 3R trade from these trapped LQ zones... also will be trying different TF to see if that makes a difference on the reliability of the trades.

I believe you are spot on in your thinking about residual orders on these types of scenarios. The way I think about it, perhaps incorrectly, is that IT create a false breakout where they trick uninformed traders into buying. The better the trick the more orders they have to overcome to reverse the market. So I figure if they build a really great level that draws lots and lots of interest that means they have to dump more sells to overcome the buyers and drop the market. If they dumped lots of sells onto the market chances are those orders were not all filled because the market moved too fast. So when we come back to revisit the area, those leftover orders are often sitting there waiting to be filled.

The only way this wouldn't be the case is if they pull the unfilled orders. Which I imagine they would only do if the market extended down to their target and it was some type of substantial bullish set-up like a QM or DM on HTF.

Gregg mentioned a concept to me a few months ago which I have applied to my trading... he uses the term 'square up'. I interpret 'squaring up' as the trapped LQ left over after the main event has occurred... tremendous capital is spent to push price in that false direction, and those open orders remain on their balance sheet as the trade progresses. Since banks and institutional funds don't use SL, they have to 'square up' or clear the orders open and dragging on their balance sheet. When price RT to that false breakout, they get out of these positions...and that is the bounce I trade.

It all seems quite logical to me... and it explains (in part) why these areas are so reactive when price returns.

1. If price engulfs this FL, which was the target, then they will want the next FL below. 2. If price arrives at this FL and then balances and shoots back up and engulfs UFL, then it means, there are no more Supply at the UFL. Therefore price will go to higher Supply level to search for more Sell orders. Once there is no more Supply. what happens is, they need to create the Fake Supply and hide their intention of wanting to Buy, therefore they will make it looks like Sell is going on, enticing sellers and breakout sellers in. Why not? =) They want the best possible price, which is this case is MPL, because that Demand has not been taken yet

In the drawing below, the price has not hit its target yet, therefore ITs are not satisfied. They will want to hit Target, before they make new decision. The risk of trading this kind of setups are, you don't know what will happen to the price as it is still in the space and anything can happen, while they play tricks. In this case, the price can go all the way up to MPL of UFL before hitting their target, CP to their level or shoot straight down to their level, if they suddenly want long. Too many options:D, therefore it will be guess work what they will do...Oh and you will not know if the LFL will hold the price or not in this case

EDIT: Ifmyante stated, that ITs dont care about profit, therefore pay attention on stops:D

Good questions! Price sometimes bounces from the mouth of a FL, and sometimes it bounces from the MPL of a FL. Often, price will bounce at both of these places.

Just because price bounces at the mouth doesn't necessarily mean we won't get a reaction from its MPL...in fact, I have noticed that a S/R (mouth) bounce frequently precedes a much larger bounce @ the FL's MPL. In these scenarios, the S/R (mouth) reaction sets up a supply/demand zone..acting as a 'trap' for traders who buy/sell the breakout.

Just a quick reminder to traders when it comes to drawing FL's. There are often multiple scales with different boxes. Quite frequently there are tiny low TF scale FL's that occur but aren't visible in your other time frames.

It is really easy to overlook these tiny FL's (I have a bad habit of doing it), but properly drawing them gives you a HUGE edge on the market. I recently went back through my losing trades to see what I did wrong. More than 50% of my losses were due to sloppy HTF drawing if FL's. It is amazing actually when you start practicing because you see how relevant those tiny FL's are.

فقط یه یادآوری سریع برای معامله‌گران دربارهٔ کشیدن FL‌ها. اغلب چند مقیاس با کادرهای مختلف هست. خیلی وقتا FL‌های کوچیک مقیاس تایم‌فریم پایین رخ می‌دن ولی تو تایم‌فریم‌های دیگه‌ات دیده نمی‌شن.

واقعاً راحته که این FL‌های کوچیک رو از قلم بندازی (عادت بدی تو این کار دارم)، ولی کشیدن درستشون بهت یه مزیت خیلی بزرگ روی بازار می‌ده. اخیراً معامله‌های بازنده‌ام رو دوباره مرور کردم تا ببینم چه اشتباهی کرده‌ام. بیش از 50% ضررهایم به‌خاطر کشیدن شل‌و‌ور FL‌های HTF بود. واقعاً وقتی شروع به تمرین می‌کنی شگفت‌زده می‌شی چون می‌بینی اون FL‌های کوچیک چقدر مرتبطن.

My answer is it depends on the importance of E:

Here is an analysis of my USD-JPY trade today: I'll start by posting the final chart, and then I will attach each of the charts showing my analysis that led up to taking the trade.

Part 1:Look left to draw the order flow as price engulfs, retraces, and forms a swap zone.

Notice how Box 3 was drawn... paying close attention to the inner FL (lower scale).

"A" shows where buyers entered the market to push price up to "B", where price took the remaining supply in Box 3 (which is a swap zone). I used the low @ "A" as the basis for Box 4, which ends up being the reason for my trade. Point C & D was confirmation that a FO would happen in to Box 4 (B&C is a RS bounce from the edge of Box 4). But, I only took the trade because of what happened in the PA between "A" and "B", specifically that B took the LQ in Box 3, which is a swap zone. No engulf happened above Box 3, which tells me all of the seller LQ was taken.

As you can see, once I complete the order flow analysis to the left, the entry is really easy. In this case, my SL was tiny.

This trade is not my typical setup, as the primary reason for taking the short was not a return to a fakeout. That said, the methodology is very similar. In my opinion, the most important part of this trade, and the reason there was sufficient order flow to bounce price, was because of how price reacted to Box 3, a swap zone. It is the same scenario for FO trades... I want to see the FO happen to a specific area of LQ at a swap zone without engulfing

Interesting Trade that I took last night on USD-CHF... great example to share. This was 17:R

I tried to clearly show where my entry and exit was. For some reason, my platform places arrows in odd places. The dotted red line is more accurate to show my entry/exit. I closed out the trade in the red circle area. My SL was about 3 pips.

Something I want to share...I have been making some changes to my strategy lately. I am becoming MUCH more interested in the approach price takes before it reaches my entry. I am learning that is more important than finding the bounce points. For example: the yellow box is pretty easy to find/draw. It's just carefully drawing FL boxes... simple.

We find areas like this all over the charts, and often they bounce price. But, we also see these FL's fail.

I am learning that whether a FL will hold depends on prices approach to the level. I want to see a structured attempt at creating supply/demand just below/above my FL box (my entry of interest). I want to see how price approaches my box, but I want price to FAIL to hit the zone. Then, I want to see a deep retrace back to some strong pocket of Liquidity before price begins to rise/drop to the entry point. These supply/demand created levels that fail to hit the entry target act as a perfect trap for traders to get in on the "breakout".

This takes some time to find on the charts... I am still practicing it. But, this USD-CHF is a perfect example. I would not have taken this trade if price hadn't formed that supply level to the immediate left of my actual entry. When I saw that false supply form, I added my limit orders and woke up to a 17:R trade!

Focus on thinking like a predator... rewire your brain to see the tricks for LQ and trading gets easier.

Hope this helps!!e

I looked at a higher TF chart, and the answer became clear to me: price was coming from a higher TF FO. See the chart Below:

On a higher TF scale, this was a FO to trap LQ for a push up... and that's a very bad time to sell. On the lower TF, this original short (at FL 3) looked good. But when you see the big picture, you see the real FO happened at FL "A".

Summary: make you aren't buying or selling against the higher time frames.

I just want to share an update with you guys about my recent progress in trading. I have been challenging myself to move away from terminology and patterns... and shift towards understanding why price often fakes out certain levels. I am learning to shift my strategy to look for opportunities to trap traders.

If you train your eyes to see the Fakeouts, you will notice they tend to occur in to areas of importance in terms of order flow.

The fakeout usually tends to serve three primary functions:

1. It spikes to areas of LQ already existing on the chart 2. It creates LQ not existing on the chart through bull traps/bear traps 3. It creates LQ pending on the chart by taking stop losses (which is LQ in the form of limit orders)

With this in mind, I shift my focus. I ask myself:

1. Which FL's are MOST likely to convince traders that the supply/demand located within is significant enough to bounce price? 2. Which FL's (or important highs or lows) are most likely to entice breakout traders when price breaches the level? 3. Which FL's are located directly above/below an area of significant LQ?

With these three questions in mind, I begin looking for a combination of these events to occur in the chart. Ideally, I want a setup in which I can say the answer to all three questions is YES

فقط می‌خوام یه آپدیت باهاتون در میون بذارم دربارهٔ پیشرفت اخیرم تو معامله. خودم رو به چالش کشیدم که از اصطلاحات و الگوها فاصله بگیرم… و به‌سوی درک اینکه چرا قیمت اغلب سطوح خاصی رو فیک‌اوت می‌کنه تغییر مسیر بدم. دارم یاد می‌گیرم استراتژی‌ام رو طوری تغییر بدم که دنبال فرصت‌های دام‌گذاشتن روی معامله‌گران بگردم.

اگه چشم‌هات رو طوری آموزش بدی که فیک‌اوت‌ها رو ببینی، متوجه می‌شی اونا تمایل دارن به نواحی مهم از نظر جریان سفارش رخ بدن.

فیک‌اوت معمولاً سه عملکرد اصلی داره:

1. به نواحی LQ که از قبل رو چارت هستن اسپایک می‌کنه 2. LQ‌ای که رو چارت نیست رو از طریق تله‌های گاوی/تله‌های خرسی می‌سازه 3. LQ سفارش‌های در انتظار رو چارت رو با گرفتن حد ضرر‌ها می‌سازه (که LQ به شکل سفارش‌های لیميته)

با این تو ذهن، تمرکزم رو عوض می‌کنم. از خودم می‌پرسم:

1. کدوم FL‌ها بیشترین احتمال رو دارن که معامله‌گران رو قانع کنن که عرضه/تقاضای داخلش به‌اندازهٔ کافی مهمه که قیمت رو برگردونه؟ 2. کدوم FL‌ها (یا سقف‌ها/کف‌های مهم) بیشترین احتمال رو دارن که وقتی قیمت از اون سطح عبور می‌کنه تریدرهای شکست رو وسوسه کنن؟ 3. کدوم FL‌ها دقیقاً بالای/پایین یه ناحیهٔ LQ معنادار قرار دارن؟

با این سه سؤال تو ذهن، شروع می‌کنم به پیدا کردن ترکیبی از این رویدادها تو چارت. در حالت ایده‌آل می‌خوام ستاپی که بتونم بگم جواب هر سه سؤال YES‌ه

This a step-by-step analysis of the simulation trade I took in Post # 2273 above.

Starting with the basics: Finding a swing low/high that includes a false break and strong follow through. I labeled this as "A". This is a HTF FL, with a false break down and a strong follow through to the upside. The false break down was the origin of the move, trapping bearish LQ to fill the longs that preceded that strong push up. A retest of that false break (bear trap) occurs, but price does not make a new low. You can see this retest in the red circle. This is important.

The next step is to identify the location where sell orders were executed at the beginning of the false move to the downside. This order flow is critically important. As you can see, in the hourly chart we are unable to discern the exact location where the bear trap originates. We need to drop down to a 15-Minute chart to see the actual FL that occurs at the break. The bets trade opportunities occur when LQ is sought by trapping LQ in the wrong direction AND when the exact break is hidden in a HTF candle. The chart below shows the execution of orders that formed the trap. That FL is labeled as "B".

After identifying the exact execution of orders forming the bear trap (B), the FL is extended to the right... all the way to the right. The details of this zone are relevant to everything we do to set up the trade.

My attention now shifts to the RT that price made to this trap, when it bounced without making a new low (I showed this reaction in the red circle on the first chart I posted in this journal entry). I am going to shift my attention to this RT. I want to draw the areas where price interacts with the "B". There will be two versions of this step... and the distinction between these two charts is really important. I will label these charts as version 1 and version 2. Take a look at Version 1 below:. I drew the FL's formed as price engulfed "B"... and labeled that FL as 'C". When "C" is engulfed, I labeled that FL "D".

The next chart is Version 2.... it is the correct way to draw this. Version 1 is drawn too broadly. When you drop to a 5-min chart, you will see the boxes are different, based on the exact location where box "B" is engulfed. The distinction is really important... and the existence of a trade setup where this occurs is good news because it increases the likelihood of your trade working. The details matter, and drawing exact FL boxes is incredibly important...I just recently realized this over the past couple of months. Look how Box C and Box D differ based on drawing the LTF boxes properly... Version 1 shows the incorrect way to draw the boxes, and Version 2 shows the correct way to draw the boxes.

I am running out of space, so I will continue this on the next post. For clarity, I am shading "D" in yellow since it is my execution box (where I will be placing my buy orders). Here is a clean chart for reference: See next post for a continuation of this trade analysis.

این یه تحلیل قدم‌به‌قدم از معاملهٔ شبیه‌سازی‌ایه که تو پست # 2273 بالا گرفتم.

شروع با مبانی: پیدا کردن یه کف/سقف سوئینگ که شامل شکست کاذب و پیگیری قویه. اینو «A» نامیدم. این یه FL تایم‌فریم بالاتره، با شکست کاذب به پایین و پیگیری قوی به بالا. شکست کاذب پایین مبدأ حرکت بود؛ LQ فروش رو به دام انداخت و اون خیز قوی به بالا خرید‌های قبلی رو هدف گرفت. بازآزمایی اون شکست کاذب (تلهٔ خرسی) رخ می‌ده، ولی قیمت کف جدید نمی‌سازه. می‌تونی این بازآزمایی رو تو دایرهٔ قرمز ببینی. این مهمه.

قدم بعدی شناسایی موقعیتی‌ه که سفارش‌های فروش تو آغاز حرکت کاذب به پایین اجرا شدن. این جریان سفارش فوق‌العاده مهمه. همون‌طور که می‌بینی، تو چارت ساعتی نمی‌تونیم محل دقیق مبدأ تلهٔ خرسی رو تشخیص بدیم. باید بریم به چارت 15 دقیقه‌ای تا FL واقعی رو ببینیم که هنگام شکست رخ می‌ده. بهترین فرصت‌های معاملاتی وقتی رخ می‌دن که LQ با دام‌گذاشتن LQ تو جهت اشتباه جست‌وجو بشه و وقتی شکست دقیق تو یه کندل HTF پنهانه. چارت پایین اجرای سفارش‌هایی رو نشون می‌ده که تله رو ساختن. اون FL با «B» برچسب خورده.

بعد از شناسایی اجرای دقیق سفارش‌هایی که تلهٔ خرسی رو ساختن (B)، FL به راست بسط داده می‌شه… تا ته راست. جزئیات این ناحیه برای همه‌چیزی که برای ستاپ معامله انجام می‌دیم مهمه.

توجه من حالا به RT‌ای می‌ره که قیمت به این تله زد، وقتی بدون ساختن کف جدید برگشت (این واکنش رو تو دایرهٔ قرمز رو اولین چارتی که تو این پست گذاشتم نشون دادم). قرارم اینه که توجه‌ام رو به این RT بدم. می‌خوام نواحی رو بکشم که قیمت با «B» در تعاملن. دو نسخه از این قدم وجود خواهد داشت… و تمایز بین این دو چارت واقعاً مهمه. این چارت‌ها رو نسخهٔ 1 و نسخهٔ 2 نام می‌ذارم. نسخهٔ 1 رو پایین ببین: FL‌هایی رو که وقتی قیمت «B» رو اینگالف کرد شکل گرفتن کشیدم… و اون FL رو «C» نامیدم. وقتی «C» اینگالف می‌شه، اون FL رو «D» نامیدم.

چارت بعدی نسخهٔ 2‌ه… روش درست کشیدن اینه. نسخهٔ 1 خیلی پهن کشیده شده. وقتی می‌ری به چارت 5 دقیقه‌ای، می‌بینی کادرها متفاوطن، بر اساس محل دقیق که کادر «B» اینگالف می‌شه. تمایز واقعاً مهمه… و وجود یه ستاپ معاملاتی که اینجا رخ می‌ده خبر خوبیه چون احتمال جواب‌دادن معامله‌ت رو افزایش می‌ده. جزئیات مهمن و کشیدن دقیق کادرهای FL باورنکردنی مهمه… من همین چند ماه اخیر اینو فهمیدم. ببین کادر C و کادر D چطور بر اساس کشیدن درست کادرهای تایم‌فریم پایین متفاوطن… نسخهٔ 1 روش نادرست کشیدن کادرها رو نشون می‌ده و نسخهٔ 2 روش درست رو.

فضام تموم می‌شه، پس این رو تو پست بعدی ادامه می‌دم. برای شفافیت، «D» رو زرد رنگ کردم چون کادر اجرامه (جایی که سفارش‌های خریدم رو خواهم گذاشت). این یه چارت تمیز برای مرجعه: ادامهٔ این تحلیل معامله رو تو پست بعدی ببین.

Starting on the left, I am drawing HTF areas of importance. This blue box (1) is important.

Now, I will draw the obvious FL that forms after price engulfs Box 1 to the upside. The herd will see this as important demand. Notice the gap between these two boxes. This is an indication that a FL may be occurring soon.

Next step: look for lower TF FL's that exist in a lower scale to identify the exact location where buyers/sellers swap. I want the exact place where opposite orders are executed. (response to Dengaima from yesterday's question)

You asked why I didn't re-draw my yellow box after price broke the LTF FL. I used to do this, but the more I practice the more I am seeing the importance of the lowest TF FL that forms after price engulfs an important area. The higher scale FL's are useful for positioning, but the real orders seem to exist in the hidden 'inner' FL's that form when price first engulfs an important zone.

This is important because the size of the FL determines when/where you draw the next engulf. That is why I prefer drawing the LTF FL first...then see what other FL's set up in the vicinity that could be used to form a FO to grab some added LQ. The LTF FL (the yellow box used in this example) is my starting point for seeing what LQ traps might set up in the area.

(پاسخ به سؤال دیروز Dengaima)

پرسیدی چرا کادر زردم رو بعد از اینکه قیمت FL تایم‌فریم پایین رو شکست دوباره نکشیدم. قبلاً این کار رو می‌کردم، ولی هرچه بیشتر تمرین می‌کنم بیشتر اهمیت FL پایین‌ترین تایم‌فریم رو می‌بینم که بعد از اینگالف قیمت از یه ناحیهٔ مهم شکل می‌گیره. FL‌های مقیاس بالاتر برای موقعیت‌دهی مفیدن، ولی به‌نظر می‌رسه سفارش‌های واقعی تو FL‌های «درونی» پنهان وجود دارن که وقتی قیمت اولین بار یه زون مهم رو اینگالف می‌کنه شکل می‌گیرن.

این مهمه چون اندازهٔ FL تعیین می‌کنه که اینگالف بعدی کجا/کی کشیده بشه. به همین دلیل ترجیح می‌دم اول FL تایم‌فریم پایین رو بکشم… بعد ببینم کدوم FL‌های دیگه تو مجاورت ستاپ می‌شن که می‌تونن برای ساختن FO به کار برن تا کمی LQ اضافه بگیرن. FL تایم‌فریم پایین (کادر زرد استفاده‌شده تو این مثال) نقطهٔ شروع منه برای دیدن اینکه چه تله‌های LQ ممکنه تو ناحیه ستاپ بشن.
More practice & more interesting patterns to see unfolding around S/R areas.

Two great opportunities to buy. Notice the green lines prior to each trade... the line sets up a demand zone which is taken out.

If you are looking to take a long trade, look for a false demand zone. If you are looking to take a short trade, look for a false supply zone. Often, these 'false' zones form just above or below an important high time frame area (target). In older posts, I talk about magnetic attraction (a concept Salivan has also mentioned).

Price is drawn to origins and important FL's at swap zones because they contain large amounts of orders. When price comes really close to one of these zones of magnetic attraction, but fails to actually hit the zone, we have a possible 'false' zone setting up.

Referring back to Post # 2349:

Here is a re-post of the chart I made:

My philosophy is an off-shoot of the main concepts taught here on RTM. Several weeks ago I began a study in to understanding why price bounces and fakes out. If you remember back to my old posts for 2016/2017 you will see I focused almost exclusively on trading the return to a fakeout that already occurred in the past. That is still a good strategy & approach to trading the market, but I always wondered how difficult it would be to trade the FO as is occurred instead of trading the return to the FO.

Trading the FO as it forms has its own benefits: mainly better RR and quick trades. Also, it's REALLY fun!

I've noticed that traders tend to form their own strategies over time as they gravitate towards a certain 'type' of trading style or methodology.

I strongly believe that price moves because of order flow. Price moves in the direction of liquidity. It is always bouncing around as the war between bears and bulls rages on. Finding where the true or 'free' or 'fresh' order flow exists is key to knowing which direction price is headed. As I mentioned yesterday, I believe true order flow exists in the tiny FL formed when price engulfs an important levels (ORFL, SWAP, FL's etc...).

Most traders on RTM know how to draw the FL boxes. They are fun to draw, and they do an excellent job of framing the market in a visual structure that draws our eyes towards the important decisions and the relevant areas of order flow.

Lately, I have been studying how to draw the FL Boxes properly. Often times, price will engulf a level and form a new FL on a LTF but price will form multiple iterations as it passes above and below that initial FL to form a HTF FL. I've heard others refer to this as an 'inner' FL and an 'outer' FL.

In my opinion (and I admit i'm still learning as I explore chart after chart after chart...) the first engulf and FL formed after price breaks an important level is the most important FL in terms of order flow. The HTF FL's that form outside of the inner FL is like a 'shell' and it's important too... but not as important the tiny inner FL.

This distinction of the inner vs outer FL is very important because we draw the boxes based on engulfs of previous boxes. Once these start getting drawn in multiple scales (fractals) we see a type of divergence or "deviation" exists between the fractals. This divergence/deviation looks like a gap of space where the distal boundaries of one FL (in one TF) are different from the distal boundaries of another FL (in a different TF). Why does this matter to us? Because if we are looking on the higher TF scale we might expect price to bounce in a particular FL where this gap exists...and price will overrun the FL making it look like price engulfed in the wrong direction when in reality it was just bouncing from the lower scale FL. Usually, these Lower scale FL's are accompanied by a false supply/demand level to create a bear/bull trap as well.

Since each new FL box depend on engulfs of preceding FL boxes, finding the exact starting point is CRITICAL. If the first FL box is incorrectly drawn, or is based on an engulf of a wrong level (or an engulf of the wrong scale) the proceeding boxes will all be wrong. Identifying the right starting point is my main focus right now...this is what I am currently working on. I will post more info when I find good examples to share.

I know this is a really hard concept to explain using words... hopefully I can find some good examples to post in my next few posts. I am still figuring this out as I go too. I am feeling highly motivated and I am excited to find out where these new discoveries will lead. Hopefully, if I am on the right track (and I think I am), I can post this information on my journal to help others as well!

متوجه شدم معامله‌گران به‌مرور استراتژی خودشون رو می‌سازن، چون به «نوع» خاصی از سبک یا روش‌شناسی معامله گرایش پیدا می‌کنن.

قویاً معتقدم قیمت به‌خاطر جریان سفارش حرکت می‌کنه. قیمت تو جهت نقدینگی حرکت می‌کنه. همیشه در حال بالا و پایین پریدنه، چون جنگ بین خرس‌ها و گاوها ادامه داره. پیدا کردن اینکه جریان سفارش واقعی یا «آزاد» یا «تازه» کجاست، کلید دانستن جهت قیمته. همون‌طور که دیروز گفتم، معتقدم جریان سفارش واقعی تو FL ریزیه که وقتی قیمت یه سطح مهم رو اینگالف می‌کنه ساخته می‌شه (ORFL، SWAP، FL‌ها و… ).

بیشتر تریدرهای RTM می‌دونن باکس‌های FL رو چطور رسم کنن. رسمشون لذت‌بخشه و کارشون رو عالی انجام می‌دن: بازار رو تو یه ساختار بصری قاب می‌گیرن که چشم ما رو به تصمیم‌های مهم و نواحی مرتبط جریان سفارش می‌کشه.

اخیراً روی این کار می‌کنم که باکس‌های FL رو درست رسم کنم. خیلی وقت‌ها قیمت یه سطح رو اینگالف می‌کنه و یه FL جدید تو تایم‌فریم پایین می‌سازه، ولی قیمت چند تا تکرار می‌سازه همون‌طور که از بالای اون FL اولیه و پایینش رد می‌شه تا یه FL تایم‌فریم بالاتر بسازه. شنیدم بقیه بهش می‌گن FL «درونی» و FL «بیرونی».

به نظر من (و قبول دارم که هنوز در حال یادگیری‌ام، چارت به چارت به چارت… ) اولین اینگالف و FL‌ی که بعد از شکست یه سطح مهم توسط قیمت ساخته می‌شه، از نظر جریان سفارش مهم‌ترین FL‌ه. FL‌های تایم‌فریم بالاتر که بیرون FL درونی شکل می‌گیرن مثل یه «پوسته» هستن و اونا هم مهم‌ان… ولی نه به‌اندازهٔ FL درونی ریز.

این تمایز بین FL درونی و بیرونی خیلی مهمه چون باکس‌ها رو بر اساس اینگالف باکس‌های قبلی رسم می‌کنیم. وقتی اینا تو مقیاس‌های متعدد (فراکتال‌ها) رسم می‌شن، می‌بینیم نوعی واگرایی یا «انحراف» بین فراکتال‌ها وجود داره. این واگرایی/انحراف شبیه شکافی تو فضاست که توش مرزهای دیستال یه FL (تو یه تایم‌فریم) با مرزهای دیستال FL دیگه (تو تایم‌فریم دیگه) فرق داره. چرا این برامون مهمه؟ چون اگه رو مقیاس تایم‌فریم بالاتر نگاه کنیم، ممکنه انتظار داشته باشیم قیمت تو FL خاصی که این شکاف توش هست برگرده… و قیمت FL رو رد می‌کنه و این‌طور به نظر می‌رسه که قیمت تو جهت اشتباه اینگالف کرده، در حالی که تو واقعیت فقط از FL مقیاس پایین‌تر برگشته. معمولاً این FL‌های مقیاس پایین‌تر با یه سطح عرضه/تقاضای کاذب همراه می‌شن تا یه تلهٔ خرسی/گاوی هم بسازن.

چون هر باکس FL جدید به اینگالف باکس‌های FL قبلی وابسته‌ست، پیدا کردن نقطهٔ شروع دقیق حیاتیه. اگه اولین باکس FL غلط رسم شده باشه، یا بر اساس اینگالف یه سطح اشتباه باشه (یا اینگالف مقیاس اشتباه)، همهٔ باکس‌های بعدی غلط خواهن بود. شناسایی نقطهٔ شروع درست، تمرکز اصلی من الانه… همین چیزیه که الان روش کار می‌کنم. وقتی مثال‌های خوبی برای اشتراک پیدا کردم، اطلاعات بیشتری می‌ذارم.

می‌دونم توضیح این مفهوم با واژه واقعاً سخته… امیدوارم بتونم چند مثال خوب برای پست‌های بعدی‌ام پیدا کنم. من هم دارم همون‌طور که پیش می‌رم کشفش می‌کنم. خیلی انگیزه دارم و هیجان‌زده‌ام ببینم این کشف‌های تازه به کجا می‌رسن. امیدوارم اگه تو مسیر درست باشم (و فکر می‌کنم هستم)، بتونم این اطلاعات رو تو ژورنالم بذارم تا به بقیه هم کمک کنه!

hoeschec wrote: Two great opportunities to buy. Notice the green lines prior to each trade... the line sets up a demand zone which is taken out.

If you are looking to take a long trade, look for a false demand zone. If you are looking to take a short trade, look for a false supply zone. Often, these 'false' zones form just above or below an important high time frame area (target). In older posts, I talk about magnetic attraction (a concept Salivan has also mentioned).

Price is drawn to origins and important FL's at swap zones because they contain large amounts of orders. When price comes really close to one of these zones of magnetic attraction, but fails to actually hit the zone, we have a possible 'false'

zone setting up.

Here is a trade I took on GU with the help of a friend:

I recently closed it out... the methodology is more or less the same:

Find a FL that can be broken, in to an area of LQ that remains somewhat hidden or obscured in some way. Consider what professional money/institutional money must to to adequately fill their orders. If pro money needs to BUY they need lots of LQ from those willing to SELL

If it looks like price is going up, nobody is going to be willing to sell...so... we look for evidence that professional money is active by looking for these tricky spots that trap LQ.
